title: Minimum Cost to Split an Array
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, find the minimum cost to split the array into non-empty subarrays.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, find the minimum cost to split the array into non-empty subarrays. The cost of a split is the sum of the importance values of each subarray. The importance value of a subarray is defined as k plus the length of the subarray after removing all elements that appear only once. Determine the minimum possible cost for any valid split.
constraints: Split nums into one or more nonempty contiguous subarrays.
A part costs k plus the number of its elements whose values occur more than once in that part.
Return the minimum total split cost.
hints: Let best[end] be the minimum cost for the prefix ending just before index end.
For each end, extend a candidate last part backward while maintaining its value frequencies and trimmed length.
A frequency changing from one to two adds two trimmed elements; every later copy adds one.
Trying every last-part start covers every possible final cut, and adding the optimal preceding prefix gives the standard optimal-substructure recurrence.
editorial: Trying every last-part start covers every possible final cut, and adding the optimal preceding prefix gives the standard optimal-substructure recurrence.

tests.explanation: Balancing new-part fees against repeated elements yields minimum total cost eight.
The optimal split has cost six.
